newsitem.title: CANADA: Royal Oak likely to close Colomac mine.
newsitem.headline: Royal Oak likely to close Colomac mine.

text.p: Royal Oak Mines Inc said on Thursday it expected to decide later this year to close its Colomac gold mine in Canada's Northwest Territories because of weakness in the gold price and other factors.
"I expect that it will be closed. But I want to stress no formal decision has as yet been made," said Graham Eacott, a spokesman for Seattle-based Royal Oak.
Colomac's cash production cost averaged US$370 an ounce last year, while the price of gold has recently fallen to around US$318 an ounce.
Colomac "is high cost. When you look at the gold price at the moment, it is not profitable," Eacott said.
He noted that the property's reserves were also diminishing and that it posed logistical hurdles because all supplies must be trucked to the remote site on a road open only a few months of the year.
Colomac produced 122,00 ounces of gold last year.
Royal Oak previously announced the closing of its Hope Brook mine in the third quarter. Eacott said none of the company's other mines was being considered for closure.
